**Risk officer assessment: ADTF**

**Refuse.** This is an operator-class coin, and the brief shows classic concentration. Bundle share and top-3 share are both 1.0, top-5 buyers hold 99.9% of early buys, and 834 SOL came from 12 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation. Sell-to-buy in that window is 0.0, so nobody has sold yet. The coin is 30 minutes old with a flat price, and the last 15 minutes show 28 sellers against 41 buyers, with net flow positive but small.

Operator-backed coins have roughly broken even, and I'd expect a sharp drop once the operator takes profit. Our $20 ticket would be a poor bet against a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost. Skip it.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying ADTF now is weak. The brief shows an OPERATOR-class coin: 834 SOL bought in the first two minutes from 12 buyers, 99.94% of that buying concentrated in the top 5 wallets, and a launch bot present. That is the pattern that tends to break even on average, and the concentration means a few wallets control the float and can exit at will.

The recent-flow numbers are the only encouraging part. Over the last 15 minutes, 10 SOL came in, the net flow was +1.83 SOL, and buyers (41) outnumbered sellers (28). The price is flat to slightly up (+0.37%), with only 0.06% drawdown from the 30-minute high. Those signs suggest some organic interest has appeared since graduation.

But the sell side is not negligible: 8.2 SOL sold against 10 SOL bought, and the 30-minute return of +4.3% is small relative to the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost. Even if demand persists for the next 30-60 minutes, a single large operator exit could erase any gain. I see no case strong enough to outweigh the base rate. Recommendation: skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution by the operator. The launch was bundled (bundle_share 1.0, top3_share 1.0, top5 buyers 99.9% of early volume), and 834 SOL came from 12 buyers in the first two minutes, well past the 500 SOL operator threshold. Operators with that much concentrated supply can sell into any bid, and the last 15 minutes already show distribution: 28 sellers against 41 buyers, 8.2 SOL sold versus 10.0 bought, and net flow of only 1.83 SOL. The 30-minute high is essentially where price sits (drawdown 0.06%), so there's no dip to buy, and at a 6M market cap the pool depth of 931 SOL means a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% costs before any exit slippage. Pass.
